newsitem.title: PARAGUAY: U.S. embassy denies supporting Paraguay's Oviedo.
newsitem.headline: U.S. embassy denies supporting Paraguay's Oviedo.

text.p: The U.S. embassy in the Paraguayan capital Asuncion denied on Monday it was backing the presidential candidacy of former army chief Lino Oviedo, accused but cleared of a heading an army revolt last year.

Oviedo, a former cavalry general, reportedly said over the weekend in a meeting with Paraguayan followers in Buenos Aires that he enjoyed U.S. support in his bid to succeed President Juan Carlos Wasmosy in next May's elections.
"The U.S. government is not backing any candidate or party in the general election to be held next year, nor in this year's primaries," a statement released by the embassy said.

"(We hope for) the victory of candidates who strongly believe in democracy and who want the country to continue to advance in modernisation and development and in international cooperation," said the statement.
"From our point of view, Gen. Oviedo, for notorious reasons, does not meet this criteria," it read.
Oviedo wants to run for president for the Colorado Party, which has run Paraguay in dictatorship and democracy for half a century, and currently heads all the opinion polls.
The general was a key figure in the 1989 coup which ended the 35-year rule of the Colorado Party dictator Gen. Alfredo Stroessner.
But he also plunged the poor, landlocked South American country into its worst crisis since the 1989 coup when he holed up in his barracks with troops and tanks last April.
The U.S. embassy warned it was a coup attempt and Oviedo was forced to step down as army chief after a tense standoff with Wasmosy. But he was later cleared of rebellion charges.

Oviedo is now vying in party primaries against Luis Argaaa, president of the Supreme Court in the dictatorship, Vice-President Angel Seifart and Carlos Facetti, another former high-level Stroessner aide.
